sanskrit: evam uktvā tu gāṅgeyo dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram dhṛtarāṣṭram athāmantrya kāle vacanam abravīt
english: Having spoken thus to Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, the son of Gaṅgā then addressed Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and at that fitting hour he spoke these words.

sanskrit: rājan viditadharmo 'si sunirṇītārthasaṃśayaḥ bahuśrutā hi te viprā bahavaḥ paryupāsitāḥ
english: O king, you are versed in dharma, and you have well resolved every doubt of meaning; for many deeply learned brāhmaṇas have you served and attended upon.

sanskrit: vedaśāstrāṇi sarvāṇi dharmāṃś ca manujeśvara vedāṃś ca caturaḥ sāṅgān nikhilenāvabudhyase
english: All the Vedas and the śāstras and the laws of dharma, O lord of men, and the four Vedas with their ancillary limbs, you comprehend entirely.

sanskrit: na śocitavyaṃ kauravya bhavitavyaṃ hi tat tathā śrutaṃ devarahasyaṃ te kṛṣṇadvaipāyanād api
english: You must not grieve, O scion of the Kurus, for what was destined had to come to pass; the secret of the gods you have heard even from Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana himself.

sanskrit: yathā pāṇḍoḥ sutā rājaṃs tathaiva tava dharmataḥ tān pālaya sthito dharme guruśuśrūṣaṇe ratān
english: As the sons of Pāṇḍu are, O king, even so are they yours in dharma; cherish them, abiding in dharma, for they delight in serving their elders.

sanskrit: dharmarājo hi śuddhātmā nideśe sthāsyate tava ānṛśaṃsyaparaṃ hy enaṃ jānāmi guruvatsalam
english: For the king of dharma, pure of soul, will abide by your command; I know him to be devoted above all to gentleness and tender toward his elders.

sanskrit: tava putrā durātmānaḥ krodhalobhaparāyaṇāḥ īrṣyābhibhūtā durvṛttās tān na śocitum arhasi
english: Your own sons were evil of soul, given over to wrath and greed, overcome by envy and wicked in conduct; for them you ought not to grieve.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ manīṣiṇam vāsudevaṃ mahābāhum abhyabhāṣata kauravaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken these words to the wise Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Kaurava then addressed the mighty-armed Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: bhagavan devadeveśa surāsuranamaskṛta trivikrama namas te 'stu śaṅkhacakragadādhara
english: O blessed Lord, god of gods and ruler of gods, honored by gods and demons alike, O Trivikrama, homage be to you, wielder of conch, discus, and mace.

sanskrit: anujānīhi māṃ kṛṣṇa vaikuṇṭha puruṣottama rakṣyāś ca te pāṇḍaveyā bhavān hy eṣāṃ parāyaṇam
english: Grant me leave to depart, O Kṛṣṇa, dweller in Vaikuṇṭha, supreme among men; the sons of Pāṇḍu are to be guarded by you, for you are their final refuge.

sanskrit: uktavān asmi durbuddhiṃ mandaṃ duryodhanaṃ purā yataḥ kṛṣṇas tato dharmo yato dharmas tato jayaḥ
english: Of old I told the foolish, dull-witted Duryodhana: where Kṛṣṇa is, there is dharma; and where dharma is, there is victory.

sanskrit: vāsudevena tīrthena putra saṃśāmya pāṇḍavaiḥ saṃdhānasya paraḥ kālas taveti ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Again and again I said: through Vāsudeva as your means of approach, my son, make peace with the Pāṇḍavas; this is the supreme hour for your reconciliation.

sanskrit: na ca me tad vaco mūḍhaḥ kṛtavān sa sumandadhīḥ ghātayitveha pṛthivīṃ tataḥ sa nidhanaṃ gataḥ
english: But that deluded one, exceedingly dull of mind, did not act upon my word; having brought slaughter upon the earth, he thereafter went to his destruction.

sanskrit: tvāṃ ca jānāmy ahaṃ vīra purāṇam ṛṣisattamam nareṇa sahitaṃ devaṃ badaryāṃ suciroṣitam
english: And I know you, O hero, to be the ancient god, the highest of seers, who together with Nara dwelt long ages at Badarī.

sanskrit: tathā me nāradaḥ prāha vyāsaś ca sumahātapāḥ naranārāyaṇāv etau saṃbhūtau manujeṣv iti
english: So Nārada told me, and Vyāsa of great austerities as well: these two, Nara and Nārāyaṇa, have been born among men.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca anujānāmi bhīṣma tvāṃ vasūn āpnuhi pārthiva na te 'sti vṛjinaṃ kiṃ cin mayā dṛṣṭaṃ mahādyute
english: Vāsudeva said: I grant you leave, Bhīṣma; attain the Vasus, O king. No taint of sin in you have I ever beheld, O greatly resplendent one.

sanskrit: pitṛbhakto 'si rājarṣe mārkaṇḍeya ivāparaḥ tena mṛtyus tava vaśe sthito bhṛtya ivānataḥ
english: You are devoted to your father, O royal seer, like a second Mārkaṇḍeya; and for that reason death stands subject to your will, bowed low like a servant.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu gāṅgeyaḥ pāṇḍavān idam abravīt dhṛtarāṣṭramukhāṃś cāpi sarvān sasuhṛdas tathā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, the son of Gaṅgā spoke this to the Pāṇḍavas and to all those led by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with their friends.

sanskrit: prāṇān utsraṣṭum icchāmi tan mānujñātum arhatha satye prayatitavyaṃ vaḥ satyaṃ hi paramaṃ balam
english: I wish now to release my life-breaths; grant me leave for this. You must strive after truth, for truth is the supreme strength.

sanskrit: ānṛśaṃsyaparair bhāvyaṃ sadaiva niyatātmabhiḥ brahmaṇyair dharmaśīlaiś ca taponītyaiś ca bhārata
english: You must ever be devoted to gentleness, self-controlled, reverent toward the brāhmaṇas, righteous in conduct, and guided by austerity and wise policy, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: ity uktvā suhṛdaḥ sarvān saṃpariṣvajya caiva ha punar evābravīd dhīmān yudhiṣṭhiram idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Having spoken thus and embraced all his loved ones, the wise one once more addressed to Yudhiṣṭhira these words.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāś caiva te nityaṃ prājñāś caiva viśeṣataḥ ācāryā ṛtvijaś caiva pūjanīyā narādhipa
english: The brāhmaṇas, and the wise especially, the teachers and the officiating priests, are ever to be honored by you, O lord of men.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā kurūn sarvān bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavas tadā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva kauravyaḥ sa muhūrtam ariṃdama
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to all the Kurus, Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu, that scion of the Kurus, then fell silent for a moment, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: dhārayām āsa cātmānaṃ dhāraṇāsu yathākramam tasyordhvam agaman prāṇāḥ saṃniruddhā mahātmanaḥ
english: He held his self steady in the fixations of yoga, each in due order; and the life-breaths of that great soul, drawn together and held in check, rose upward.

sanskrit: idam āścaryam āsīc ca madhye teṣāṃ mahātmanām yad yan muñcati gātrāṇāṃ sa śaṃtanusutas tadā tat tad viśalyaṃ bhavati yogayuktasya tasya vai
english: And this wonder occurred in the midst of those great souls: whatever part of his limbs the son of Śaṃtanu then released, that very part, as he was joined in yoga, became free of its arrows.

sanskrit: kṣaṇena prekṣatāṃ teṣāṃ viśalyaḥ so 'bhavat tadā taṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitāḥ sarve vāsudevapurogamāḥ saha tair munibhiḥ sarvais tadā vyāsādibhir nṛpa
english: In an instant, before their watching eyes, he became wholly free of arrows; and seeing this, all were amazed, led by Vāsudeva, together with all those sages headed by Vyāsa, O king.

sanskrit: saṃniruddhas tu tenātmā sarveṣv āyataneṣu vai jagāma bhittvā mūrdhānaṃ divam abhyutpapāta ca
english: His self, held fast by him in all its seats, then broke through the crown of his head and sprang up into heaven.

sanskrit: maholkeva ca bhīṣmasya mūrdhadeśāj janādhipa niḥsṛtyākāśam āviśya kṣaṇenāntaradhīyata
english: Like a great meteor, O lord of men, it issued forth from the region of Bhīṣma's head, entered the sky, and in a moment vanished from sight.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa nṛpaśārdūla nṛpaḥ śāṃtanavas tadā samayujyata lokaiḥ svair bharatānāṃ kulodvahaḥ
english: Thus, O tiger among kings, the king, the son of Śaṃtanu, upholder of the line of the Bharatas, was then united with his own worlds.

sanskrit: tatas tv ādāya dārūṇi gandhāṃś ca vividhān bahūn citāṃ cakrur mahātmānaḥ pāṇḍavā viduras tathā yuyutsuś cāpi kauravyaḥ prekṣakās tv itare 'bhavan
english: Then, taking timber and many varied fragrances, the great-souled Pāṇḍavas, and Vidura, and Yuyutsu the Kaurava, built the funeral pyre; the others stood by as onlookers.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu gāṅgeyaṃ viduraś ca mahāmatiḥ chādayām āsatur ubhau kṣaumair mālyaiś ca kauravam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira and the deeply wise Vidura, both of them, covered the Kaurava son of Gaṅgā with fine linen and garlands.

sanskrit: dhārayām āsa tasyātha yuyutsuś chatram uttamam cāmaravyajane śubhre bhīmasenārjunāv ubhau uṣṇīṣe paryagṛhṇītāṃ mādrīputrāv ubhau tadā
english: Then Yuyutsu held over him a splendid royal parasol; Bhīmasena and Arjuna, the two of them, plied the bright yak-tail fans; and the two sons of Mādrī took up the place at the headdress.

sanskrit: striyaḥ kauravanāthasya bhīṣmaṃ kurukulodbhavam tālavṛntāny upādāya paryavījan samantataḥ
english: The women of the lord of the Kauravas, taking up palm-leaf fans, fanned Bhīṣma, born of the Kuru line, on every side.

sanskrit: tato 'sya vidhivac cakruḥ pitṛmedhaṃ mahātmanaḥ yājakā juhuvuś cāgniṃ jaguḥ sāmāni sāmagāḥ
english: Then they performed for that great soul the funeral rites according to ordinance; the officiating priests poured oblations into the fire, and the singers of the Sāman chanted the Sāman hymns.

sanskrit: tataś candanakāṣṭhaiś ca tathā kāleyakair api kālāgaruprabhṛtibhir gandhaiś coccāvacais tathā
english: Then with billets of sandalwood, and with kāleyaka aloeswood, and with black aloe and other fragrances, high and low alike,

sanskrit: samavacchādya gāṅgeyaṃ prajvālya ca hutāśanam apasavyam akurvanta dhṛtarāṣṭramukhā nṛpāḥ
english: having covered over the son of Gaṅgā and kindled the fire, the kings led by Dhṛtarāṣṭra made the rightward circumambulation around him.

sanskrit: saṃskṛtya ca kuruśreṣṭhaṃ gāṅgeyaṃ kurusattamāḥ jagmur bhāgīrathītīram ṛṣijuṣṭaṃ kurūdvahāḥ
english: And having performed the rites for the best of the Kurus, the son of Gaṅgā, those foremost of the Kurus, upholders of the Kuru line, went to the bank of the Bhāgīrathī, frequented by sages.

sanskrit: anugamyamānā vyāsena nāradenāsitena ca kṛṣṇena bharatastrībhir ye ca paurāḥ samāgatāḥ
english: Followed by Vyāsa, by Nārada and Asita, by Kṛṣṇa, by the women of the Bharatas, and by such townsfolk as had gathered there,

sanskrit: udakaṃ cakrire caiva gāṅgeyasya mahātmanaḥ vidhivat kṣatriyaśreṣṭhāḥ sa ca sarvo janas tadā
english: those best of kṣatriyas, and all that assembled folk, then offered the water-libation for the great-souled son of Gaṅgā, according to ordinance.

sanskrit: tato bhāgīrathī devī tanayasyodake kṛte utthāya salilāt tasmād rudatī śokalālasā
english: Then the goddess Bhāgīrathī, when the water-rite for her son had been performed, rose up out of those waters, weeping, lost in grief.

sanskrit: paridevayatī tatra kauravān abhyabhāṣata nibodhata yathāvṛttam ucyamānaṃ mayānaghāḥ
english: Lamenting there, she addressed the Kauravas: Hear, O sinless ones, what truly came to pass, as I now tell it.

sanskrit: rājavṛttena saṃpannaḥ prajñayābhijanena ca satkartā kuruvṛddhānāṃ pitṛbhakto dṛḍhavrataḥ
english: Endowed with royal conduct, with wisdom and noble birth, an honorer of the Kuru elders, devoted to his father, firm in his vows—

sanskrit: jāmadagnyena rāmeṇa purā yo na parājitaḥ divyair astrair mahāvīryaḥ sa hato 'dya śikhaṇḍinā
english: he whom of old Rāma, son of Jamadagni, could not vanquish even with his celestial weapons—that one of mighty valor has today been slain by Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: aśmasāramayaṃ nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ mama pārthivāḥ apaśyantyāḥ priyaṃ putraṃ yatra dīryati me 'dya vai
english: Surely, O kings, this heart of mine is wrought of iron-hard stone, that even now it does not burst within me, beholding no more my beloved son.

sanskrit: sametaṃ pārthivaṃ kṣatraṃ kāśipuryāṃ svayaṃvare vijityaikarathenājau kanyās tā yo jahāra ha
english: He who, single-charioted, in battle defeated the whole assembled royal warrior-host at the bride-choosing in the city of Kāśi, and carried off those maidens—

sanskrit: yasya nāsti bale tulyaḥ pṛthivyām api kaś cana hataṃ śikhaṇḍinā śrutvā yan na dīryati me manaḥ
english: he who in strength had not one equal anywhere on earth—hearing that he has been slain by Śikhaṇḍin, how is it that my mind does not break apart?

sanskrit: jāmadagnyaḥ kurukṣetre yudhi yena mahātmanā pīḍito nātiyatnena nihataḥ sa śikhaṇḍinā
english: He, that great soul, by whom the son of Jamadagni was hard-pressed in battle on Kurukṣetra—he has been slain, and with no great effort, by Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhaṃ bahu tadā vilapantīṃ mahānadīm āśvāsayām āsa tadā sāmnā dāmodaro vibhuḥ
english: As the great river thus lamented at length in such wise, the mighty Dāmodara then consoled her with gentle words.

sanskrit: samāśvasihi bhadre tvaṃ mā śucaḥ śubhadarśane gataḥ sa paramāṃ siddhiṃ tava putro na saṃśayaḥ
english: Take comfort, gentle lady; do not grieve, O fair to behold. Your son has attained the supreme perfection—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: vasur eṣa mahātejāḥ śāpadoṣeṇa śobhane manuṣyatām anuprāpto nainaṃ śocitum arhasi
english: This one of great splendor was a Vasu, O lovely one, who through the blemish of a curse had come to dwell in the state of a man; for him you ought not to grieve.

sanskrit: sa eṣa kṣatradharmeṇa yudhyamāno raṇājire dhanaṃjayena nihato naiṣa nunnaḥ śikhaṇḍinā
english: This very one, fighting by the dharma of the kṣatriya on the field of battle, was slain by Dhanaṃjaya; it was not he who was struck down by Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaṃ hi kuruśārdūlam udyateṣuṃ mahāraṇe na śaktaḥ saṃyuge hantuṃ sākṣād api śatakratuḥ
english: For Bhīṣma, that tiger among the Kurus, with weapon raised in the great battle, not even Śatakratu himself could have slain in combat face to face.

sanskrit: svacchandena sutas tubhyaṃ gataḥ svargaṃ śubhānane na śaktāḥ syur nihantuṃ hi raṇe taṃ sarvadevatāḥ
english: By his own free will your son has gone to heaven, O fair of face; for not all the gods together could have slain him in battle.

sanskrit: tasmān mā tvaṃ saricchreṣṭhe śocasva kurunandanam vasūn eṣa gato devi putras te vijvarā bhava
english: Therefore, O best of rivers, do not grieve for the delight of the Kurus; to the Vasus has this son of yours gone, O goddess—be free of your fever of sorrow.

sanskrit: ity uktā sā tu kṛṣṇena vyāsena ca saridvarā tyaktvā śokaṃ mahārāja svaṃ vāry avatatāra ha
english: Thus addressed by Kṛṣṇa and by Vyāsa, that best of rivers, O great king, cast off her grief and descended back into her own waters.

sanskrit: satkṛtya te tāṃ saritaṃ tataḥ kṛṣṇamukhā nṛpāḥ anujñātās tayā sarve nyavartanta janādhipāḥ
english: Having honored that river, the kings led by Kṛṣṇa, all those lords of men, took their leave of her and then turned back homeward.
